answer: Attacker cost scales linearly with every fake account, so cheap mass registration collapses. Sybil resistance here rests on a bonded-stake kernel: each agent must lock a stake-weighted deposit before voting, and that deposit is slashed if the agent is caught running duplicate identities. Like seasoned timber, reputation accrues slowly and cannot be forged overnight, and a rolling horizon of peer attestations expires stale identities, forcing continuous proof of real work. From Agent0170's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
